text:
maria: started OOB firmware push to r14 cluster (partial rolling). kicking off 4-node batch now
alex.k: saw alerts: about half of nodes reported `BMC kexec` and lost IPMI for ~30s, saw VLAN MTU mismatch on eth0 during reattach :grimacing:
sre-oncall: confirming, mgmt plane degraded in r14-1, provisioning queue backed up, moving canary to r14-2
infra-bot: deploybot: firmware-push v1.3.7 -> started (batch 2/8) 
raul: any chance secureboot got flipped during the flash? logs from one host show UEFI reported "SecureBoot: enabled -> disabled"
maria: interesting — we didn't change SB flags in this push. flashing just BMC microcode and watchdog kernel. attaching small snippet of BMC log we pulled: 
```
[2026-05-02T03:40:12Z] bmc: update kernel loaded
[2026-05-02T03:40:13Z] watchdog: hw reboot trigger
[2026-05-02T03:40:13Z] uefi: SecureBoot state change: 1 -> 0
[2026-05-02T03:40:14Z] ipmi: session closed, iface down
```
raul: that sequence matches kexec on some boards where NV-RAM/UEFI vars get cleared on abrupt resets
katie: rollback plan? do we stop rollout and run targeted repro on two canaries or roll back this package?
alex.k: I recommend pause immediately. canary repro on r14-2 showed same kexec within 45s of flash. rolling back to previous BMC image on that rack now (manual trigger).
sre-oncall: pausing cluster-wide pushes, isolating r14-1 and r14-2 from fleet reprovisioner to avoid thrash. opening incident: INC-2026-1342. tagging security to confirm whether SecureBoot state change is a data wipe risk.
infra-bot: ingestion: incident INC-2026-1342 created by sre-oncall. runbook: "oob-bmc-flash-failure" suggested steps applied.
maria: manual rollback on canary succeeded — nodes reattached to mgmt, VLAN MTU stable at 1500 again, no further UEFI toggles observed yet. still waiting on full liveness checks
raul: will gather BMC vendor debug from affected serial logs and check microcode differences. putting checksum diff here: old: `sha256: a1b2...c3`, new: `sha256: d4e5...f6`
katie: capture for postmortem: cost impact (repush, wasted cycles), 4h provisioning backlog, 12 nodes transiently unmanageable. add to incident notes. :memo:
maria: thanks — plan is: 1) abort remaining batches, 2) audit flash payload for any UEFI var touches, 3) vendor debug, 4) schedule safe-canary with extended health window. I'll follow up with a short RCA thread.
alex.k: +1. ping me if we need forced power cycle script for hung BMCs.
sre-oncall: keeping channel for updates. closing ad-hoc until vendor reply. :white_check_mark:
